# Feature: Final door — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #100 (Final door) from Keys and Locks before it is used in real levels. Effect: needs one key of each colour held. Unique: checks all colours held at once, consumes none. Useful: a finale that tests breadth, not a single colour. Source status in the candidate file is 'trial'.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** needs one key of each colour held.

**So that** a finale that tests breadth, not a single colour.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Final door for the first time in its teaching room (mech-100-final-door-room). Teaching moment: First room: the final door at the end of a corridor, with one colour's key visible back the way you came. A player who walks straight to the door is told by nothing happening that a colour is missing and faces the whole corridor back, which teaches that the door is an inventory check to be prepared for rather than a lock to be opened on arrival. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: The door checks your inventory, bot included, for at least one key of each colour at the same time
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: If you hold them all it opens permanently and consumes none of them
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: If any colour is missing it does nothing

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Final door's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-100-final-door-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/keys-and-locks.yml mechanic #100.
